candidates.title: Delayed Handover: Agreeing the Next Step
candidates.goal: Acknowledge your colleague's constraint, justify a practical next step, and confirm you both leave with the same understanding of the decision.
candidates.user_role: The project lead who needs the handover to move forward and wants to agree a realistic plan with your colleague.
candidates.ai_role: A colleague on the delivery team who is waiting on the client's data and is worried about committing to a new date.

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Concede that the colleague's concern is reasonable before offering a different view.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: Your colleague says the client still hasn't sent the figures and the delay isn't their fault. How do you respond before suggesting a different plan?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if the colleague has already fully accepted the delay and no concession is needed.
implicit_targets.sentence_frame: To be fair, [colleague's valid concern], but [your different view].

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Use a shared fact or constraint to justify a proposed next step.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: You both agree the client's figures won't arrive until Thursday. What practical next step do you propose, and what shared fact supports it?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if no shared fact or constraint has been established to base a recommendation on.

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Confirm a shared understanding of the decision before ending the discussion.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: Before you both hang up, how would you check that you're leaving with the same understanding of what was decided?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if the call has already ended or the decision is still unresolved.
implicit_targets.sentence_frame: Before we finish, I want to make sure we're on the same page about [decision].

candidates.title: Rescheduling the Client Review
candidates.goal: Recognise the supplier delay as a fair point, propose a rescheduled review based on that fact, and confirm you both agree on the new arrangement.
candidates.user_role: The team member who owns the review deck and needs to agree a new date with your manager.
candidates.ai_role: The manager who is under pressure from the client and needs a clear, justified plan.

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Acknowledge that the other person's point is reasonable before presenting a different view.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: Your manager points out the client is expecting the review tomorrow and the delay looks bad. How do you respond before proposing a different arrangement?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if the manager has already agreed the delay is unavoidable and no concession is needed.
implicit_targets.sentence_frame: To be fair, [manager's valid point], but [your different view].

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Base a recommendation on an agreed fact or constraint.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: The supplier report only arrived this morning. What do you recommend for the review, and what fact makes that sensible?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if no agreed fact or constraint has been established to justify a recommendation.

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Check that both people understand the decision the same way before parting.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: As you part ways, how would you make sure you both understand the new arrangement the same way?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if the conversation has already ended or no decision has been reached.
implicit_targets.sentence_frame: Just to check, are we on the same page about [arrangement]?

candidates.title: Sprint Planning: Handling the Missing Sign-off
candidates.goal: Accept the product owner's concern as fair, propose a revised sprint scope based on the pending sign-off, and confirm shared understanding of the plan.
candidates.user_role: The developer who needs to agree a realistic sprint scope with the product owner.
candidates.ai_role: The product owner who is anxious about the release date and the pending legal sign-off.

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Concede that the other person's worry is legitimate before offering a different perspective.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: The product owner says the release date is fixed and slipping is not acceptable. How do you respond before suggesting a different scope?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if the product owner has already accepted the revised scope without objection.
implicit_targets.sentence_frame: To be fair, [product owner's valid concern], but [your different perspective].

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Use a shared constraint to justify a proposed change of plan.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: Legal sign-off is still pending. What change to the sprint scope do you propose, and what fact supports it?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if no shared constraint has been agreed to base a proposal on.

implicit_targets.communicative_function: Confirm that both parties share the same understanding of the agreed plan.
implicit_targets.trigger_question: Before the meeting ends, how would you confirm you both understand the revised scope the same way?
implicit_targets.skip_when: Skip if the meeting has already ended or the scope is still undecided.
implicit_targets.sentence_frame: Before we wrap up, let's make sure we're on the same page about [plan].
